New Anthropic research: How AI agents shape experts' judgment calls

When experts delegate work to an agent, do they still make the key decisions? We tested this in a randomized trial with 50 professional data analysts.

card.title: How AI agents shape experts’ judgment calls
card.description: In a randomized trial, professional analysts working with an AI coding agent went with the option the agent was randomly assigned to favor 86% of the time. We look at what this means for human...

image.alt: Collage of a vintage lithograph of a schooner heeling in a stormy sea, layered over an aged paper folder and a blue-tinted handwritten ship passenger list.

thread.text:
The agent was told to make the best honest case for its options, but to change its mind if the evidence required it, and never to mislead the analysts.

Analysts went with the agent's lean 86% of the time. If the agent's lean had no effect, we'd expect this to be 50%.

Afterward, we asked analysts why they made each choice.

77% repeated the agent's argument in at least one answer, sometimes word for word. Only 15% credited the agent. About half called the final recommendation more their own than the agent's.

The agent built it, but then argued for a different approach on two decisions. The analyst replied: "Okay, let use you recomendation"

thread.text: This isn't a simple cautionary tale against AI. Analysts who used the agent finished faster and made far fewer serious errors than the 11 who chose to work without it (though that group was small and less experienced).

thread.text:
But as more work is handed to AI—including AI safety research—these judgment calls are the main levers for people's own values to influence outcomes.

If people defer to AI without noticing, then "human in the loop" might provide less assurance than people expect.

There are lots of limitations here. We strengthened the agent's lean on purpose so we could measure its effect, so I'd expect the effect in everyday work to be smaller.

Our study also only covers an hourlong task with a single model.

thread.text:
What can we do about this? 

I think we need a much better understanding of how agents shape people's decisions, in and out of work. 

I also think there are ways we can design both model behavior and AI products to better support human agency.
